findings.claim: The id assertion is a bare substring check for "1", so it would pass with the wrong id or a message that merely contains the digit 1.
findings.failure_scenario: The code reports the task's position, a count, or the date part of some other value containing '1' instead of task['id']; the test still passes because the only task has id 1 and the check is `"1" in line`.
findings.rule: AC-1 (the line contains the task's id and its bad due value)
findings.evidence: assert "1" in lines[0] and "soon" in lines[0]

findings.claim: No test covers the open-task qualifier: a done task with a malformed due, or a mix of tasks, is never exercised, so removing the `not task["done"]` guard or the reporting of the correct task among several would go unnoticed.
findings.failure_scenario: A change makes list --overdue fail on a done task with due 'soon' (or report the first task rather than the bad one); the only fixture is a single open task with id 1, so every test still passes.
findings.rule: AC-1 ("an open task ... has a malformed stored due date")
